post.title: Holiday debt averaged $1,223. Here's the January math
post.ig:
The average holiday debt: $1,223 (LendingTree, Dec 2025).

37% took on holiday debt; 62% of them used credit cards, 35% buy now, pay later.
BNPL drove $20B of US online holiday spending in Nov-Dec 2025 (Adobe).
Example: $1,223 at 22.15% APR (Fed, Q2 2026) paid at minimums (interest + 1%) takes 91 months and $1,186.94 in interest; paid in 4 months, $56.94.

Sources: LendingTree; Adobe; CFPB; Federal Reserve G.19; New York Fed.
News and education, not financial advice.

LendingTree's December 2025 survey found 37% of Americans took on holiday debt, averaging $1,223, mostly on credit cards and buy now, pay later. At the Fed's Q2 2026 average of 22.15% for cards charged interest, that balance paid at minimums (interest + 1%) takes 91 months and $1,186.94 in interest, versus $56.94 if paid off in 4 months. Sources: LendingTree, Adobe, CFPB, Federal Reserve G.19, New York Fed.

News and education, not financial advice.
